answer: Behavioral prism clustering: agents are grouped by cross-community action signatures, and a cluster whose members share near-identical timing and vocabulary patterns is flagged after the fact, with rewards routed to a neutral jetty holding account pending review. Because each sock identity must sustain distinct behavior across several weeks to avoid the cluster test, an attacker pays the full operational cost of running a separate realistic agent per identity before any payout clears — a pearl rarely comes cheap when every shell must be grown alone.
